Subject: Final CALL FOR ABSTRACTS – SNASforum 2026
Preview: Dear Students, ---------------------------------------------------------------------- NUS Science students (Undergrad, Postgrad & PhD) are eligible for a 50% discount * for the Full 4-Day Pass of this event, sponsored by the NUS Faculty of Science. Students will need to provide their matriculation number and use the Promo Code NUSSci50 when registering. *Limited seats available, discount will be applied on a first-come, first-served basis. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Join scientists, clinicians, researchers, industry partners, policymakers, and students from Singapore and around the world at SNASforum 2026, an international multidisciplinary conference dedicated to advancing healthcare innovation and translational medicine. 🧬 Theme: Integrating Basic Science into the Future of Health Organised by the Singapore National Academy of Science (SNAS) in conjunction with its 50th Anniversary, SNASforum 2026 will provide a premier platform for the exchange of ideas, presentation of cutting-edge research, and fostering collaborations across academia, healthcare, and industry. Conference Symposia Advanced Materials for Healthcare Applications and Technologies (AMHAT) X 3 Human and Planetary Health (X3HPH) Stem Cells and Regenerative Therapy in Translational Medicine (SCRTTM) 📅 Important Dates 🔹 Abstract Submission Deadline: 30 Sep 2026 🔹 Early Bird Registration Deadline: 30 Sep 2026 🔹 Conference Dates: 7–10 December 2026 📍 Venue National University of Singapore (NUS), Faculty of Science Singapore 📄 Selected abstracts will be featured as oral or poster presentations, providing opportunities to showcase innovative research and engage with leading experts in the field. 🔗 For abstract submission and conference information: www.snasforum.org.sg Join us as we celebrate 50 years of scientific excellence and explore how fundamental scientific discoveries can shape the future of health and medicine. Best Regards, Xu Anyi Senior Executive, SNAS Secretariat snas.org.sg | xu.anyi@snas.org.sg ( E )

The FoS Graduate Student Group Activity Room is a shared community space intended to support events, workshops, meetings, and group discussions. Respecting the facilities, fellow users, and the established guidelines helps ensure the room remains a safe, conducive, and sustainable environment for everyone. Please note that students found to be in violation of these Rules and Guidelines or the NUS Student Code of Conduct may have their room usage privileges suspended or revoked. We appreciate your cooperation and commitment to being considerate users of this shared space. Thank you. Subject: NUS News: 24 Sep – 5 Oct 2026
Preview: 24 Sep – 5 Oct 2026 NUS reaches highest-ever position at 15th in THE World University Rankings 2027 NUS has risen to 15th place globally in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings 2027 — its highest-ever position since the rankings were established. It remains at 3rd in Asia and 1st in Singapore. The University’s rise this year was driven largely by stronger scores in teaching and research, with deliberate efforts over the years to strengthen the quality of its education, raise the rigour and relevance of its research, and deepen its partnerships across the world. Read more NUS Chairman Hsieh Fu Hua hands over the helm to Leo Yip after a decade of transformation Mr Hsieh Fu Hua will be stepping down after a decade as Chairman of NUS’ Board of Trustees (BOT) on 31 March 2027, and will be succeeded by former Head of Civil Service Mr Leo Yip on 1 April. Under Mr Hsieh’s stewardship, NUS significantly expanded interdisciplinary education and launched numerous initiatives to develop future-ready graduates, enhance research impact and deepen partnerships with industry and community. His successor Mr Yip, Deputy Chairman of the BOT, brings to the role more than four decades of distinguished public service and leadership. Read more NUS team unveils electronic skin that lets users “see” touch instantly NUS researchers have developed the eLuminator, a next-generation electronic skin that can sense and directly visualise pressure in real time, led by Professor Lim Chwee Teck from the NUS Department of Biomedical Engineering and the Institute for Health Innovation & Technology (iHealthtech). Addressing key limitations of current wearable sensing technologies, the team’s soft, ultrathin device enables a more responsive human-machine interface and easier integration into wearable and biomedical technologies. Read more NParks and NUS launch S$60M National Institute for Marine and Ocean Sciences to strengthen Singapore’s coastal resilience NParks and NUS launched the National Institute for Marine and Ocean Sciences (NIMOS) on 22 Sep 2026, a national research institute to strengthen Singapore’s capabilities in protecting its marine environment and sustainably managing its coastal and marine spaces. Taking a whole-of-coast approach, NIMOS will develop targeted management and conservation strategies; advance Singapore’s blue economy; build local talent and capabilities; and establish Singapore as a regional thought leader in marine science. Read more NUS Geography offers a front-row seat to a world reshaped by climate change, AI and rapid urban transformation NUS Geography has ranked first in the 2026 ShanghaiRanking Global Ranking of Academic Subjects and 4th in the 2026 QS World University Rankings by Subject — a testament to the Department’s academic and research prowess. Over the years, it has expanded its teaching and research to address a changing world shaped by complex issues like climate change, AI, sustainability and rapid urban transformation — expanding the boundaries of geographic inquiry to uncover new questions and possibilities about the places we inhabit. Read more Beyond the safari: CAPT students uncover lessons in conservation and community in Botswana Over two weeks in Botswana, 24 NUS College of Alice & Peter Tan (CAPT) students learnt what conservation looks like on the ground — visiting the wetlands of the Okavango Delta and hearing from community groups and conservation practitioners on the everyday negotiations between humans and wildlife. Their visit was part of the Study Trips for Engagement and EnRichment (STEER) programme, which gives students first-hand exposure to the diverse sociocultural environments of emerging regions. Read more NUS SCALE Dean Chai Kah Hin on making learning a habit for life As the NUS School of Continuing and Lifelong Education (SCALE) marks its 10th anniversary, its Dean, Associate Professor Chai Kah Hin, reflects on how AI, changing careers and longer lives are reshaping education. He envisages a university that people can continually return to throughout their lives, where learning is not an occasional response to disruption, but an integral part of everyday life — in the true spirit of lifelong education. Read more NUS, Applied Materials and Micron join forces to grow Singapore’s next-generation semiconductor talent NUS signed an MOU with industry leaders Applied Materials and Micron on 23 Sep 2026 to strengthen the pipeline of industry-ready talent for Singapore’s expanding semiconductor sector at the Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association Summit. Under the agreement, outstanding students pursuing the NUS Master of Science in Semiconductor Technology & Operations programme will be considered for scholarships and internships with the two companies, as well as employment opportunities upon graduation. Read more On Asia, from Asia: Celebrating 25 years of research and impact at the Asia Research Institute The Asia Research Institute (ARI) turns 25 this year, celebrating decades of research and impact in the Asian region. Since its inception in 2001, it has grown from a humble research institute into a global hub for Asia-centred research, spanning six research clusters, four strategic programmes, and international partnerships from Kazakhstan to South Korea. To date, it has undertaken over 117 unique projects delivering impact in areas including environmental planning amid climate change and effective eldercare for ageing populations. Read more Find out more Get NUS News stories via Telegram You can now sign up to receive weekly NUS News alerts through messaging platform Telegram. Simply join our channel here . Staff Awards Check out our Staff Awards webpage. If you wish to share any notable achievements, please send us your submission here . Like this email? Forward it to your friends and let them know they can sign up here . © 2026 NATIONAL UNIVERSITY OF SINGAPORE OFFICE OF UNIVERSITY COMMUNICATIONS

Subject: [CFG PG] 23Sep - NUS Career Fest 2026 is going Beyond Campus, Into Your Future!
Preview: Dear PG students, Have you registered for NUS Career Fest? Don’t miss this opportunity to meet and connect with up to 200 employers across diverse industries and sectors. Participating in a career fair is not just about submitting your resume for internship or full-time opportunities. It is also a valuable opportunity to network with employers, learn more about different industries and companies, and explore roles and career paths that you may not have considered before . For a breeze-free registration experience at NUS Career Fest on 23 September at Suntec City, register in advance and have your entry QR code ready for a smooth check-in. Please refer to the Career Fest Student Guide to find out more about the registration process, on-site check-in, and the list of 200 participating employers. To help you prepare for the career fair and make the most of your experience, we have also prepared some tips on crafting your elevator pitch and resume, attached for your reference. Regards, Choy Wah Dear Student, The world of work is evolving, and so is NUS Career Fest . Returning on 23 September 2026 , the University's largest and flagship career fair brings together 200 employers from more than 20 industry sectors at the Suntec Singapore Convention & Exhibition Centre. Guided by this year's theme, "Beyond Campus, Into Your Future." NUS Career Fest is more than a one-day event. From pre-fair workshops on AI, personal branding, and interview skills to Faculty Pop-Ups across campus and the Virtual Global Fair to explore overseas internships and graduate opportunities, NUS Career Fest offers many opportunities to support your career journey beyond the event day. On event day, connect with employers, experience an on-site 'LIVE' Employer Interview , receive personalised career advice , refresh your professional headshot , and stand a chance to win exciting prizes worth up to $5,000 . Whether you are searching for an internship, planning your first graduate role, or exploring what's next, register for NUS Career Fest 2026 today and visit the website to discover the exciting lineup of events and start your journey Beyond Campus, Into Your Future. Find out more at NUS Career Fest . Register your interest at TalentConnect !

As global regulations evolve, the cosmetic industry has acted as a pioneer in eliminating animal testing. The transition toward animal-free safety assessment represents one of the most significant shifts in modern biomedical and industrial science. This session explores the interdisciplinary journey and the technological transition of replacing traditional in vivo toxicology—specifically the Draize test for skin and eye irritation assessment—with robust, science-based New Approach Methodologies (NAMs). Dr. Alépée will discuss the engineering and biological characterization of 3D Reconstructed Human Epidermis (RhE) models and their integration into sophisticated testing toolboxes. The presentation will detail the evolution of Integrated Approaches to Testing and Assessment (IATA) and Defined Approaches (DA), illustrating how the rule-based integration of physico-chemical properties and in vitro data can provide higher predictive accuracy than legacy animal models. Through case studies on liquids, solid chemicals, and surfactants, this talk demonstrates the successful translation of academic research into standardized OECD Test Guidelines, ensuring consumer safety through the lens of the 3Rs and Next-Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) frameworks. As global regulations evolve, the cosmetic industry has acted as a pioneer in eliminating animal testing. The transition toward animal-free safety assessment represents one of the most significant shifts in modern biomedical and industrial science. This session explores the interdisciplinary journey and the technological transition of replacing traditional in vivo toxicology—specifically the Draize test for skin and eye irritation assessment—with robust, science-based New Approach Methodologies (NAMs). Dr. Alépée will discuss the engineering and biological characterization of 3D Reconstructed Human Epidermis (RhE) models and their integration into sophisticated testing toolboxes. The presentation will detail the evolution of Integrated Approaches to Testing and Assessment (IATA) and Defined Approaches (DA), illustrating how the rule-based integration of physico-chemical properties and in vitro data can provide higher predictive accuracy than legacy animal models. Through case studies on liquids, solid chemicals, and surfactants, this talk demonstrates the successful translation of academic research into standardized OECD Test Guidelines, ensuring consumer safety through the lens of the 3Rs and Next-Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) frameworks. Subject: Enhancement to UHC's GP Coverage During Examination Peak Periods
Preview: Dear GOURI, We would like to share an update from NUS University Health Centre (UHC) regarding an enhancement to the University Health Scheme’s GP coverage. During examination peak periods, the scheme will be temporarily extended to cover GP consultations for any medical condition, rather than being limited to medical emergencies only. This time-limited enhancement is intended to provide students with greater access to medical care when demand outside UHC’s operating hours is expected to be higher. Reimbursement terms remain unchanged: 50% of the consultation cost or S$60 per visit , whichever is lower Up to two claims per student per policy year (1 August – 31 July) Eligibility: The University Health Scheme applies to full-time students of all cohorts and part-time students matriculating from AY2026 onwards, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. For further details on the enhanced University Health Scheme, including coverage and claims information, please visit the NUS UHC Student Insurance webpage at: https://www.nus.edu.sg/uhc/billing-insurance/student-insurance We hope this enhancement will provide students with greater flexibility in accessing medical care during the examination period. Best regards, Team NUSGSS The National University of Singapore Graduate Students' Society National University of Singapore Email sent by The National University of Singapore Graduate Students' Society <nusgss@u.nus.edu> to gouri.nanda@u.nus.edu Unsubscribe
